name: Notion
summary: Self-serve public integration, no review needed to start. A Marketplace listing is separate and optional. The catches are the Basic-auth token exchange, rotating refresh tokens, and that users only share the pages they pick.

difficulty.label: Easy
difficulty.why: No approval. Setup is one form. The tricky parts are implementation details, not process.

approval.detail: The docs say Marketplace submission or review is not required to start authorization. The Marketplace listing has its own review, whose timeline I could not find.

agentCan: Build the authorize URL with owner=user and a state value
Write the token exchange with the Basic auth header (base64 of client_id:client_secret)
Implement refresh handling that replaces both tokens on every refresh
Test against your own workspace once you paste credentials
youMustDo: Create the integration in the Notion developer portal (login required)
Choose the 'Any workspace' installation scope. It cannot be changed afterwards
Copy the client secret and keep it out of source control

steps.title: Create a public integration
steps.detail: In the Notion developer portal, create a new OAuth integration. Enter your redirect URI(s) in the OAuth configuration section.

steps.title: Set installation scope to Any workspace
steps.detail: Do this at creation. The docs state it can't be changed later, so a mistake means a new integration with a new client ID.

steps.title: Copy credentials
steps.detail: Client ID, client secret and the authorization URL are on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Send users to authorize
steps.detail: GET /v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, and an optional state.

steps.title: Exchange the code
steps.detail: POST /v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (client_id:client_secret), body grant_type=authorization_code and code. If the authorize URL carried redirect_uri, or you registered more than one URI, the token request must include it too.

steps.title: Handle refresh
steps.detail: Refresh at the same endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token. Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so store both every time.

requirements: A Notion account that can create integrations

gotchas.detail: Access is limited to pages the user shares with the connection. Your agent may find an empty workspace after a successful OAuth flow, so add an onboarding step asking users to pick pages.
A refresh returns a new refresh token, so store the new pair every time.

gotchas.issue: Token lifetime not documented on this page
gotchas.detail: The authorization page doesn't state how long access tokens last. Plan to refresh on 401.

blockers.fix: Create a new integration. The scope is fixed at creation.
Send the same redirect_uri you used in the authorize step.
